title: Why Being Good At Your Job Isn't Enough
strength: Strong core tension: competence vs perceived expertise.
risk: Needs one more vivid real-world failure/success contrast early to maximize cold-viewer retention.

title: How To Find Your Niche Without Making Yourself Too Small
strength: Resolves a common fear and gives a useful niche-as-entry-strategy frame.
risk: Middle section is concept-dense; one recurring case study would improve narrative propulsion.

title: How To Position Yourself As An Expert From Zero
strength: Practical evidence-over-label thesis with strong credibility discipline.
risk: Broad topic and familiar advice; needs a sharper transformation arc or unusual case example.

title: The Content Strategy That Makes People Remember You
strength: Highly series-relevant thesis with strong recognition-vs-volume distinction.
risk: Minor risk of abstraction; visual examples should carry the middle.

title: Why Writing A Book Can Make You The Expert
strength: Credible, nuanced authority-building argument that avoids “book = expert” hype.
risk: Narrower addressable audience and lower cold-feed urgency; hook should foreground a surprising business payoff.

title: How To Reposition Yourself When Your Business Changes
strength: Excellent memory-gap tension and a clear observable outcome for repositioning.
risk: Needs disciplined visuals to avoid becoming a talking-head lecture.

title: A Good Business Starts With The Right Business Model
strength: Strong counterintuitive hook and concrete unit-economics stress test.
risk: Keep financial examples simple enough for fast comprehension.

title: Your Ideal Customer Is Not Everyone
strength: Operationalizes customer definition around need/context/signal rather than demographics.
risk: Very familiar headline territory; requires fresher examples and stronger pattern interruption.

title: People Don't Buy Your Product They Buy The Promise
strength: Strong translation from product features to lived outcome with credibility guardrails.
risk: Theme is common in marketing content; differentiation must come from examples and visual proof.

title: How To Build An Offer People Actually Want
strength: Clear friction-reduction system and strong buyer-journey utility.
risk: Avoid stacking too many checklist items without concrete before/after demonstrations.

title: Stop Improving The Marketing Fix The Product
strength: Excellent diagnostic tension and falsifiable validation mindset.
risk: No material editorial blocker; maintain brisk pacing through the diagnostic sections.

title: Attention Is Not Conversion
strength: Best-in-pack framing: instantly understandable, measurable, and highly relevant to creators/businesses.
risk: Only risk is over-explaining the funnel after the thesis is already proven.

title: Why Selling Feels Difficult
strength: Human tension around money/rejection gives the topic emotional accessibility.
risk: Needs concrete scenes/dialogue to keep it from drifting into generalized coaching.

title: Sales Without Chasing Everyone
strength: Strong systems framing and useful prospecting path with explicit stop rules.
risk: Concept load is high; show one prospect moving through the path rather than only explaining stages.

title: How to Differentiate When Everyone Offers the Same Thing
strength: Excellent anti-adjective hook and a genuinely useful mechanism-based differentiation thesis.
risk: No major story blocker; prioritize visual comparisons to maintain momentum.

title: Build a Signature Method People Can Understand and Buy
strength: Very strong consultant-specific problem, clear mechanism, and commercial payoff.
risk: Could use one memorable named example of a weak method becoming a strong one.

title: The Psychology of Memorable Business Storytelling
strength: Narrative topic naturally supports narrative delivery and visual variety.
risk: Must demonstrate the storytelling principles rather than merely enumerate them.

title: The Expert Business Flywheel: Positioning → Offer → Content → Sales → Retention
strength: Excellent capstone architecture and strong series-level coherence.
risk: As a cold standalone video it is dense; best published after viewers know the component ideas.

title: Being Good Isn't Enough
strength: Immediate competence-vs-perception conflict with a clear takeaway.
risk: Still slightly lecture-like; add a visual/client-choice beat in the first third.

title: Expertise Vs Perception
strength: Strong “delete the label” test creates an interactive viewer challenge.
risk: Keep proof examples visually distinct to avoid list fatigue.

title: What Do People Remember You For
strength: Excellent audience-participation test with measurable external feedback.
risk: No material story blocker.

title: Selling To Everyone Is The Problem
strength: Clear specificity thesis and strong contrast example.
risk: Familiar advice; hook needs a more surprising consequence to outperform generic niche content.

title: Why Smaller Niches Can Make You Bigger
strength: Counterintuitive headline plus a strong “wedge, not prison” payoff.
risk: No material story blocker.

title: Market Problem Solution Test
strength: Useful three-part diagnostic that viewers can apply immediately.
risk: Framework is valuable but visually static; needs a concrete worked example.

title: You Can't Just Call Yourself An Expert
strength: Evidence-over-title thesis is credible and brand-safe.
risk: Opening is predictable; needs a more specific failed-profile example or sharper claim.

title: Three Signals To Build From Zero
strength: Good beginner framework with ethical proof-building.
risk: Feels like standard three-tip content; needs a stronger novelty mechanism or mini-case.

title: Your Website Has Five Seconds

risk: No material story blocker.

title: Stop Posting Random Content

title: The Goal Is Recognition Not Views

risk: No material story blocker.

title: Make Other People Talk About Your Expertise

title: You Don't Need A Publisher

title: Don't Write A Book About Everything You Know

title: One Book Can Become Fifty Pieces Of Content

title: Your Audience Remembers The Old You

title: If You Stop Working Does Your Revenue Stop Too

title: Views Are Not Sales
